items.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: And I was doing the Jimmy Dean Show, and they came. And I said, “Hey, I can write that. Something like that.” And I wrote the song with another name. I called it Ladybug. [laughs] And I take that to Lou Levy, the publisher, the boss of Duchess. And he said, “Toots,

it’s great but it ain’t Bluesette,” you know. [laughs] I know [inaudible]. And he had a representative in Los Angeles. The brother of Les Brown. Les Brown, the band… He had a brother or cousin, something Brown, was operating the office of Duchess in Los Angeles. And at that time, they say, “Oh, there was this guy, Herb Alpert, starting.”
